claims.claim: On the same spawn schedule, the commit-charge guard sheds and a rescue spawn still succeeds before unguarded process creation fails at commit_limit.
The guard and live probe read commit_charge (Committed_AS) and available_commit, not working set (Active/VmRSS). A working-set guard is silent in the commit-exhaustion failing state.
The load test does not drive this host to its real commit ceiling. Host freeze is refused; evidence is the simulated kernel plus a 64MiB untouched mmap.

legacy_root.question: Failure class :11327. Measured root cause on this box: the freeze is COMMIT charge (RAM+pagefile) exhaustion, not RAM OOM - Task Manager hides it and Event 2004 is the smoking gun. Target: a load test that drives commit charge toward the limit and asserts the guard sheds load BEFORE process creation fails, plus a probe that reads commit charge rather than working set.
legacy_root.title: Commit-exhaustion guard: process creation freezes before RAM is exhausted
